feedback.problem:
Let
$T=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 8 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}]$
be the standard matrix of the linear transformation $T.$ Then $T$ maps ${R}^{2}$ onto
feedback.worked_solution:
Notice that $T$ has proportional rows, and yet $T$ is not the zero matrix. 

Therefore, $\text{rank}(T)=1$ and $T$ maps ${R}^{2}$ onto a line that passes through the origin.

Moreover, the line must pass through the origin $(0,0)$ and the points $(-4,1)$ and $(8,-2),$ which are defined by the columns of the matrix $T.$ 

Computing the slope $m$ of this line, we get

$$
m=\frac{-2-1}{8-(-4)}=-\frac{1}{4}.
$$

 

Therefore, $T$ maps ${R}^{2}$ onto the line $y=-\frac{1}{4}x.$
